items.followUp: Why does a passenger jerk forward when a moving bus suddenly stops?

rubric.why: The passenger’s body tends to preserve its state of motion due to inertia.
rubric.how: Award for naming inertia as the cause.

rubric.why: As the bus changes direction, the passenger’s body tends to continue in its original straight-line direction, making the passenger move outward relative to the bus.
rubric.description: Explains the body’s tendency to continue in its original direction.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the body continues in its original direction or along a straight line as the bus turns.

modelAnswer: When a bus takes a turn, its direction changes, but the passenger’s body tends to continue in its original straight-line direction due to inertia of motion.
Therefore, the passenger appears to move outward relative to the bus.

items.followUp: What is meant by an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: The defining property of a rigid body is that the distances between its particles remain unchanged.
rubric.description: States that the distance between the body’s particles remains constant.
rubric.how: Award for stating that distances between particles remain constant.

rubric.why: A rigid body retains its shape and size.
rubric.description: States that the body’s shape and size do not change.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the shape and size remain unchanged.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body in which the distance between any two particles remains constant.
Therefore, its shape and size remain unchanged when forces act on it.
